Benchling’s mission is to unlock the power of biotechnology. The world’s most innovative biotech companies use Benchling’s R&D Cloud to power the development of breakthrough products and accelerate time to milestone and market.

drive the integration of liquid biopsy approaches within the context of our portfolio, provide input into the clinical trial protocols

Configure, test, commission, maintain, and upgrade industrial control systems throughout their lifecycle.
Collaborate with project leaders, process engineers, operators, and other stakeholders throughout all project phases.
Coordinate technicians and junior engineers and supervise contractors during implementation and commissioning activities.
Manage technical procurements, service contracts, and interactions with industrial suppliers.

Evaluate emerging technologies and engineering methodologies, and contribute to technical studies internal EN-CV-CL standards improvement.

Adaptyv is building an automated lab that lets AI agents run biology experiments. 

We're entering the era of agentic science where AI models can now design novel proteins, propose hypotheses, and iterate on experimental results. But they can't run the experiments themselves - that's still a manual, months-long process. We're building the infrastructure that gives AI agents access to the physical world.

We are one of the fastest growing biotech companies, trusted by leading biopharmas, frontier AI labs, and the techbio companies pushing the field forward. This is a rare chance to help advance some of the most important work happening in biotech today.

Our automated lab is powered by a deep software + hardware stack: lab instruments worth millions of USD reverse-engineered into API-controllable hardware, dozens of devices orchestrated through complex workflows, full observability on everything that happens in the lab, processing pipelines for messy physical-world data, and AI systems that troubleshoot production results and accelerate assay development.

We’re growing rapidly and are hiring for talented people to scale and support the massive demand for AI-driven wet lab experimentation.


ABOUT THE ROLE

This is not a lab technician position. This is a senior scientist who owns assay quality, data QC and controls, and production troubleshooting across the entire experimental pipeline.

The production team runs 150+ experiments per month across expression, BLI, SPR, thermostability, and enzyme activity. When something goes wrong (failed expression, anomalous binding data, instrument artifacts), this person diagnoses the root cause and fixes it. As the assay and instrumentation portfolio expands, this person translates new R&D methods into production-ready protocols, builds robust methods that junior technicians can execute reliably, and designs comprehensive controls that enable automated QC and data processing.

This is a player-coach position. You will still run experiments personally, especially as you integrate into the lab, but you will also elevate the whole team's capabilities.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Troubleshoot production failures across the full pipeline. A batch of proteins isn't expressing: is it the construct design, the expression system, or the media? BLI sensorgrams look noisy: is it the sensor tips, the sample prep, or an instrument issue? You figure it out, fix it, and make the cause easier to identify next time.

 - Develop and document SOPs for new assays as the portfolio expands. Take methods from the R&D team and make them production-ready: robust, reproducible, and executable by junior technicians without hand-holding.

 - Mentor a growing production team. Set quality standards, review data, train new hires, and build a culture where people flag problems early instead of hiding them.

 - Work at the intersection of biology, automation, and QC. Collaborate with researchers, laboratory technicians, and automation engineers on protocol optimization for work cells, and with software on LabOS protocol integration.

 - Own the relationship between assay science and throughput. The easy version of every assay doesn't scale, and the scalable version often sacrifices quality. You find the right tradeoff.


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - Deep hands-on expertise in protein production: expression (E. coli, mammalian, cell-free), purification (IMAC, SEC), and biophysical characterization (BLI and SPR at minimum). This isn't negotiable. You need to have done this work yourself, at volume.

 - PhD in protein biochemistry, biophysics, or a relevant field, plus 3–5 years in a production or development role at a CRO, foundry, or high-throughput lab. Academic postdocs count if the work was high-throughput and production-oriented.

 - Experience with high-throughput workflows. You're comfortable with 96-well plates and liquid handlers, not just single-column purifications. You've optimized protocols for scale, not just for one perfect result.

 - Mentorship mindset. You've managed or trained junior scientists before. You enjoy teaching and get satisfaction from watching your team grow.

 - Troubleshooting instinct. When data looks wrong, your first impulse is to understand why, not to rerun the experiment and hope it works.

 - Quality-obsessed but pragmatic. You care deeply about data quality, but you also understand that production has deadlines and sometimes "good enough" is the right call.

 - Bridge between R&D and production. You can speak both languages: the exploratory mindset of research and the reproducibility demands of production.


DETAILS

 - Location: Lausanne, Switzerland (on-site)

 - Type: Full time

 - Start date: ASAP

Adaptyv is building an automated lab that lets AI agents run biology experiments. 

We're entering the era of agentic science where AI models can now design novel proteins, propose hypotheses, and iterate on experimental results. But they can't run the experiments themselves - that's still a manual, months-long process. We're building the infrastructure that gives AI agents access to the physical world.

Our automated lab is powered by a deep software + hardware stack: lab instruments worth millions of USD reverse-engineered into API-controllable hardware, dozens of devices orchestrated through complex workflows, full observability on everything that happens in the lab, processing pipelines for messy physical-world data, and AI systems that troubleshoot production results and accelerate assay development.

We’re growing rapidly and are hiring for talented people to scale and support the massive demand for AI-driven wet lab experimentation.


ABOUT THE ROLE

Our lab produces binding data faster than any one person can look at it. Runs come off the Gators and the Carterra, go through our processing pipeline, and land in a review queue. Somebody with real judgment then has to decide: is this curve real? Is that a fit artifact or a genuine two-state binding event? Does this replicate get delivered, or does the sample get re-run? That person is you.

The second half of the job is talking to the customer about it. When a design team gets a plate back and three of their best predictions look like non-binders, they want to talk to someone who can explain why: reference subtraction, avidity, an off-rate at the edge of what the instrument resolves, or simply a bad protein. You'll be that person, on the call, sharing your screen, walking through sensorgrams.

This is a role for a scientist who is very good at kinetics and also likes people. If you like one but not the other, you'll be unhappy here.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Review the binding data coming out of the lab. Every SPR and BLI run passes through our processing pipeline and then to human review, and you're the expert eye on the output. You decide what gets delivered, what gets flagged, and what gets re-run.

 - Judge the curves, not just the numbers. A clean-looking Kd on a bad fit is worse than no number at all. You know the difference between a real off-rate and a drifting baseline, and you can say why.

 - Review data from our other assays too: thermostability, expression, developability, enzyme activity. Binding is the core of the role but it isn't all of it.

 - Talk to customers about their results. Deliverable walkthroughs, follow-up questions, and the awkward conversation when the data doesn't say what they hoped. You explain what we measured, how confident we are, and what to do next.

 - Turn review into experimental design. When something needs a re-run, you decide what changes: orientation, regeneration, concentration series, or a switch from BLI to SPR for the sensitivity.

 - Analyze at the batch level, not just the sample level. With hundreds of results per experiment, you should be writing a script to find the pattern rather than clicking through a queue. Systematic drift, a bad reference channel, or a target lot behaving differently than the last one shows up in aggregate long before it shows up in any single curve.

 - Feed what you learn back into the pipeline. When you catch a case where automation passed something it shouldn't have, or failed something it shouldn't have, that becomes a concrete requirement for the software team.

 - Work closely with production (what actually happened in the lab), QC (systematic quality), and customer success (the relationship around the science).


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - MSc / PhD in biochemistry, biophysics, or a relevant field, plus 3+ years working hands-on with binding kinetics.

 - Deep SPR and BLI experience. Biacore, Carterra, Octet, Gator: the platform matters less than the fact that you've run these assays, troubleshot them, and interpreted a lot of data from them. You've seen enough sensorgrams to know immediately when one is lying to you.

 - Real fitting judgment. 1:1 vs. bivalent, when steady-state is appropriate and when it isn't, how mass transport and avidity distort a result. You can defend a Kd, or refuse to report one.

 - Strong data analysis skills. Python or R, enough to pull a few hundred results out of a database, fit them, plot them, and find the outliers. This role generates too much data to review by hand.

 - You use AI tools seriously. We run on Claude Code and similar tooling internally, and the people who get the most done here are the ones who reach for it by default: writing the analysis script, querying the database, building the one-off dashboard. You don't need to have done this before, but you need to want to. If your instinct is that real scientists do it by hand, this isn't the place.

 - A self-starter who works independently. Nobody is going to hand you a prioritized queue every morning. You'll figure out what matters most, go do it, and tell us what you found.

 - A fast learner. Our platform, our assays, and our software change constantly. You'll be handed unfamiliar tools and expected to be productive with them quickly.

 - Startup speed, not academic pace. Experiments ship to paying customers on deadlines. Getting a good answer this week beats a perfect one next quarter, and we'd rather flag an ambiguous result than sit on it.

 - Comfortable in front of customers. Many are PhD-level scientists at pharma companies and AI labs, and they will push back. You should enjoy that conversation rather than dread it.

 - Able to explain hard things simply. Some customers are biophysicists. Some are ML researchers who have never touched a pipette. You adjust without condescending to either.

 - Honest about uncertainty. When the data is ambiguous, you say so, to us and to the customer. We would much rather flag a weak result than ship a confident wrong one.

 - Familiarity with other biophysical or functional assays (DSF, HPLC, plate-based activity assays) is a plus.


DETAILS

 - Location: Lausanne, Switzerland (on-site)

 - Type: Full time

 - Start date: ASAP

We are offering a position in the Physics Software Engineering section of the Computing for Experiments group in the CERN IT department (IT-CE-PSE) on Performance Software Engineering in the realm of high energy physics data simulation.
The work on this post will be carried out in the context of the NextGen project, a collaboration between the LHC experiments and the CERN Research and Computing Departments. NextGen explores the use and impact of high-performance computing architectures in data simulation and data processing for the LHC experiments with a focus on the upcoming High Luminosity (HL-LHC) data taking phase at the CERN Large Hadron Collider.
The simulation of particle collisions is one of the main consumers of computing resources for LHC experiments. Given the expected increase in the required statistics, accuracy and complexity for future simulation, and to stay within the forecasted computing budget, the throughput of simulation software packages needs to increase substantially.
The successful candidate will join a team of software engineers and physicists that addresses this challenge. Together, you will speed up software packages for Monte Carlo (MC) event generation with a focus on the Madgraph event generator suite. Current and future tasks tackled by the team are at the intersection of theoretical/computational physics and computer science. In order to profit from the latest computing hardware, adaptations or re-engineering of software in aspects such as data structures, parallelisation of the workflow or task scheduling are needed. This work is guided by the requirements of experimental analyses and takes into account the latest developments in theoretical predictions.
In case of interest, training on data science, programming languages, software engineering concepts and computing architectures is available and can be provided via various training programs.

Analyse and profile existing simulation code bases and develop strategies for improving their throughput.
Implement latest software engineering concepts, leveraging on compute accelerators such as GPUs, modern CPU architectures and heterogeneous compute platforms.
Interact and collaborate with experts in the theory, experimental physics and software engineering communities at CERN and world-wide.
Supervise students on software development tasks and projects.

Preferably a PhD in Theoretical or Particle Physics or Master's Degree with equivalent work experience with a strong background in numerical simulation.

The next generation of experiments, the HL-LHC upgrade of CMS and the Future Circular Collider, needs event reconstruction that is fast, accurate and portable across CPUs and GPUs. Every reconstruction algorithm and every machine-learning model is trained and judged against the simulation truth. Today that truth is stored in static, detector-specific objects. Each object is pre-grouped for one purpose, it cannot be navigated, and it separates calorimeter truth from tracker truth.
CERN has built a prototype that replaces them. It is one navigable, event-level graph of the generator and simulation history, with calorimeter and tracker hit indices on top. Reconstruction code then reasons in terms of stable physics abstractions: particles, vertices, decay branches and hits.
You will make this the truth model of the future. You will generalise the prototype into an experiment-independent library, you will bring it into the FCC software stack, and you will use it to build the next reconstruction: graph algorithms and modern machine learning for clustering, particle flow and particle identification, and reliable matching between reconstructed objects and truth. You will join the EP-FCC group, and you will work on both CMS and FCC-ee.
Your responsibilities:
Generalise the CMS MC-truth graph into a detector-independent and experiment-independent library. Separate the graph data model, the navigation API and the hit index from the experiment data-format bindings.
Develop the bindings. Keep the CMSSW binding working, and add a binding for the FCC stack (Key4hep, EDM4hep, Gaudi), so that both experiments build the same graph from their own simulation output.
Extend the data model. Add multi-surface boundary crossings, sparse association storage, and a reduced hit-index layout. Handle pileup consistently.
Develop the reconstruction-to-truth association. Extend the adaptive branch associator, which selects the truth level that best matches a reconstructed object, and validate it on merged topologies such as converted photons, bremsstrahlung and early hadronic interactions.
Define what is reconstructible. Derive it from the truth graph and the detector description, using cell granularity, energy and time resolution, readout thresholds and two-object separation.
Apply portable graph algorithms and advanced machine learning, for example graph neural networks and transformers, to reconstruction tasks in CMS (HGCAL and TICL) and in FCC detectors: clustering, linking, particle flow and particle identification.
Build the training datasets and the labels from the truth graph. Define the metrics, calibrate the model outputs, and check the model before it feeds reconstruction.
Contribute the code to the official repositories of CMS and of the FCC software stack, with unit tests, documentation and code review.
Present the results in CMS and FCC meetings, in software forums and in publications.
This role includes team supervision responsibilities.
Your profile:
A Master's Degree or a PhD in Physics, Computer Science, Applied Mathematics or a related field.
Demonstrated experience with modern C++ in a large, shared and peer-reviewed codebase, for example CMSSW, Gaudi or Key4hep.
Demonstrated experience with time-aware event reconstruction and detector simulation in a high-energy physics experiment.
Demonstrated experience with heterogeneous and portable computing, for example Alpaka, SYCL, CUDA or HIP.
Experience with Python and with at least one machine-learning framework, preferably PyTorch.
Experience with graph and clustering algorithms.
Experience with git, code review and continuous integration.
Skills:

Detector simulation.

The Position
Job Summary

As Portfolio & Programme Manager within Global Data & Digital Solutions (GDDS), you will play a strategic role in shaping, prioritising and orchestrating the global data and digital transformation portfolio across Sites Network.

GDDS is responsible for establishing trusted data foundations, scalable digital capabilities, and AI-enabled intelligence across Sites Network and SHE.

In this role, you will connect strategic ambitions with execution by establishing an integrated portfolio of initiatives, strengthening governance and ensuring transparency on priorities, investments, dependencies and business outcomes.
Working across global functions, sites, and RDT, you will foster alignment, facilitate informed decision-making and ensure that data and digital investments deliver measurable and sustainable business value.

The Opportunity

You will have the opportunity to shape and mature portfolio and programme management within a growing global function, bringing strategic focus, structure and transparency to a diverse landscape of data, digital and AI initiatives.

Strategic Portfolio Management

Establish and manage an integrated GDDS portfolio, ensuring alignment with strategic ambitions and business priorities across Sites & Sustainability.
Develop and implement portfolio prioritisation frameworks based on strategic relevance, business value, resource capacity, dependencies and implementation readiness.
Shape and maintain an integrated portfolio roadmap, identifying opportunities for synergies, standardisation and scalability across global functions and sites.
Provide leadership with a consolidated view of portfolio priorities, investments, delivery progress, risks and strategic trade-offs.
Programme Orchestration & Strategic Execution
Orchestrate strategic, cross-functional programmes spanning data management, digital solutions, AI adoption and operational transformation.
Translate strategic priorities into coordinated programme roadmaps, milestones, governance structures and measurable outcomes.
Manage cross-programme dependencies, critical risks and escalations to maintain alignment and execution momentum.
Partner with solution business owners, digital solution owners and RDT to coordinate execution while maintaining clear accountability for individual solution delivery.

Portfolio Governance & Value Realisation

Establish and continuously improve portfolio and programme governance, including decision forums (Governance Council), prioritisation processes, reporting standards and escalation mechanisms.
Define portfolio performance indicators and value realisation measures to assess strategic progress, delivery effectiveness and business impact.
Develop transparent, decision-oriented reporting that supports leadership in making informed investment and resource allocation decisions.
Monitor portfolio health, identify emerging risks and recommend corrective actions or strategic adjustments when required.

Stakeholder Alignment & Transformation

Build strong partnerships across global business functions, sites and RDT to align priorities and foster effective collaboration.
Facilitate cross-functional decision-making and resolve competing priorities in a complex, fragmented environment.
Support organisational readiness and adoption by ensuring that programme objectives, business ownership and expected outcomes are clearly defined.
Promote consistent portfolio and programme management practices while balancing global standards with local business needs.

Who You Are

You are a strategic, structured and collaborative professional who thrives at the intersection of business strategy, technology and transformation. You bring clarity to complexity, influence across organisational boundaries and maintain a strong focus on business outcomes.
University degree in Business Administration, Information Technology, Engineering or a related discipline.
Experience in strategic portfolio management, programme management or business transformation within a global, matrixed organisation.
Demonstrated ability to establish portfolio governance, prioritisation frameworks, integrated roadmaps and performance management practices.
Proven experience orchestrating complex, cross-functional transformation programmes involving multiple business and technology stakeholders.
Strong understanding of data management, digital platforms, analytics and AI, with the ability to translate technological opportunities into business value.
Experience working with business functions and IT delivery organisations in agile, traditional or hybrid delivery environments.
Familiarity with established portfolio and programme management methodologies such as PMI, or SAFe is an advantage.

Strategic thinker: Connects organisational ambitions with portfolio priorities and actionable execution plans.
Outcome-oriented: Focuses on measurable business value rather than solely on project milestones and deliverables.
Influential collaborator: Builds alignment and drives decisions through strong relationships and credibility, without relying on formal authority.
Structured and analytical: Brings transparency to complex portfolios and translates information into actionable leadership insights.
Pragmatic and adaptable: Balances global governance with the flexibility required in a decentralised organisation.
Confident communicator: Engages effectively with senior leadership and diverse stakeholders, facilitating clear decisions and constructive dialogue.
Transformation-minded: Embraces change, challenges established ways of working and continuously seeks opportunities to improve organisational effectiveness.
You are motivated by the opportunity to shape a strategic global capability, connect data and digital ambitions with business execution, and contribute to lasting transformation across Sites & Sustainability.

Job Description SummaryNovartis BioMedical Research (BR) is the innovation engine of Novartis that collaborates across the company and beyond, focusing on powerful new technologies that have the potential to help produce therapeutic breakthroughs for patients. Translational Medicine (TM) is the clinical research arm of Novartis BR, and includes about 900 associates globally. TM plays a pivotal role in bringing innovative medicines to patients, by building on research advances to develop new therapies, and bridging drug discovery and clinical application.
